first.rationale: Competitor entry pricing creates an immediate acquisition threat among price-sensitive SMBs, and the inherited record suggests targeted pricing previously lifted qualified acquisition and revenue. Verify that result and the onboarding alternative before committing; use a guarded, segment-targeted test because discounting can reduce long-term value or attract lower-quality demand.

mid.rationale: Run the shortened-onboarding experiment. Its verified record improved completion by 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and increased 30-day retention by 3%, directly addressing the current onboarding decline while supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Do not use promotional pricing: its verified revenue lift came with a 12% 30-day retention decline, making it unsuitable for the primary objective.

final2.rationale: Do not react to the competitor's deeper cut with promotional pricing: the verified prior discount cohort had 12% lower 30-day retention, which conflicts with sustainable qualified revenue. Launch a tightly scoped referral incentive to established customers instead; it previously added qualified revenue without measurable retention harm. This will not directly resolve price-driven churn, so limit the test, monitor referral quality and retention, and address at-risk SMB conversations through non-experimental customer-success actions.
